status: dependency plan only; no Lean completion is inferred
goal: Schedule the beginning of the four textbook libraries by mathematical dependency rather than cover-to-cover order, so genuinely identical lower-level Lean lemmas are proved once and reused with explicit adapters.
scope: Lectures on Optimization Chapters 1-2, with Chapter 9 duality pulled forward when OT Chapter 1 needs it
Boumal Chapters 1-3 minimal first-order geometry, because Sampling Chapter 2.5 depends on it

policies.dependency_over_book_order: A later source chapter may be mined early for one shared prerequisite when another textbook needs it. This never marks that later chapter complete.
policies.exact_match: One source-neutral canonical Lean declaration, then source-facing wrappers if needed.
policies.near_match: Factor only the mathematically identical core; keep norm, measure, manifold, extended-value, or convention adapters explicit.
policies.false_friend: Do not merge results merely because they use the words convexity, gradient, geodesic, flow, entropy, or Wasserstein.
policies.ownership: Shared foundations live in TechnicalLemmas or an audited Mathlib/upstream dependency, never inside a route-specific theorem file.
policies.chapter_status: Reusing or pulling forward a prerequisite does not advance the source chapter status except for the exact source-facing theorem that was audited.

textbook_windows.role: canonical textbook spine, distinct from SampleWiki frontier work
anchors: Chapter 1 §§1.1-1.5: stochastic calculus, semigroups, OT geometry, Wasserstein gradient flow

Chapter 9: Fenchel duality, pulled forward only for the shared duality core

Boumal Chapter 3: Embedded geometry, first order; pulled forward as needed by Sampling §2.5

nodes.title: Euclidean, inner-product and matrix floor
nodes.target: Coordinates, norms, inner products, symmetric/PSD matrix facts and quadratic energies with conventions fixed once.
nodes.boundary: Do not package manifold tangent geometry into this node.

nodes.title: Differential, gradient, chain-rule and Hessian floor
nodes.target: Source-neutral Fréchet derivative/gradient/chain-rule interfaces; Hessian inequalities retain their exact ambient spaces.
nodes.boundary: Riemannian gradients are adapters through a metric, not aliases for Euclidean gradients.

nodes.title: Convexity, strong convexity, subgradients and log-concavity
nodes.target: One canonical Euclidean convex core: convexity inequalities, strong convexity, subgradients and quadratic-growth consequences; log-concavity is an explicit density/potential adapter.
nodes.boundary: Mixture convexity, geodesic convexity and displacement convexity remain different predicates.

nodes.title: Measures, integration, maps and finite-moment floor
nodes.target: Probability normalization, map/pushforward, product measures, marginals, integrability and moment bookkeeping.
nodes.boundary: Markov kernels and couplings get their own layers; a measurable map is not a stochastic kernel.

nodes.title: Couplings, marginal constraints and Wasserstein metric core
nodes.target: Coupling membership, marginal transfer, finite p-moment cost, Wasserstein symmetry/triangle and deterministic pushforward couplings before either textbook builds local copies.
nodes.boundary: Optimal-coupling existence, Brenier maps and displacement geodesics are downstream theorems, not part of the minimal metric API.

nodes.title: Convex conjugacy and duality pulled forward for transport
nodes.target: Conjugacy, Fenchel inequalities and the exact no-gap/attainment interfaces needed by Kantorovich duality.
nodes.boundary: Pulling this core forward does not claim Optimization Chapter 9 is formalized and does not identify Fenchel and Kantorovich duality without an adapter.

nodes.title: Gradient-flow energy dissipation and scalar contraction lemmas
nodes.target: Chain rule along curves, energy derivative identities, Grönwall-type decay and strong-convexity contraction in the exact ambient setting.
nodes.boundary: Do not create a universal GradientFlow class that pretends Euclidean ODE, Riemannian flow and Wasserstein flow are definitionally the same.

nodes.title: Markov kernels, semigroups, generators and Dirichlet forms
nodes.target: Kernel composition, semigroup laws, generator-domain contracts and integration-by-parts/Dirichlet interfaces reusable by later sampling/frontier work.
nodes.boundary: This lane is sampling-owned on the front-loaded critical path; OT Chapter 1 and Optimization Chapter 1 must not wait for it.

nodes.title: Minimal manifold first-order adapter
source_anchors: Boumal Ch.3 Embedded geometry: first order
nodes.target: Tangent spaces, differential, Riemannian metric and gradient interfaces with one explicit Euclidean/embedded adapter.
nodes.boundary: Retractions, Hessians, geodesic convexity and global manifold results remain later layers unless a source theorem needs them.

nodes.title: Empirical measures, Lipschitz observables and concentration floor
source_anchors: Sampling §2.4 Concentration of Measure and Isoperimetry
nodes.target: Empirical-measure bookkeeping, expectation/probability bounds and reusable Lipschitz concentration interfaces; OT-specific chaining and sampling-specific isoperimetry stay separate.
nodes.boundary: The observation count n in OT statistics is not a sampler oracle-query count.
